key_insight: CompressionBench studies whether coding agents can autonomously compress pretrained LLMs while preserving their behavior under a smaller storage budget. The provided abstract introduces the task but does not report performance results.
problem_solved: Testing whether AI coding agents can turn model compression into an autonomous workflow while operating within storage, inference-environment, and time constraints.
method: Frame LLM compression as a terminal-based task for a coding agent.
Provide a source checkpoint, storage limit, inference environment, and time budget.
Task the agent with constructing compressed weights that retain the source model's behavior.
impact: This work offers a concrete way to study agents' ability to improve the efficiency of models used by future AI systems. For practitioners, it targets automated model-size reduction, though the supplied excerpt does not establish achieved savings or quality retention.
visual_elements: Workflow diagram: source checkpoint → coding agent → compressed model.
Constraint icons: storage budget, inference environment, and time limit.
Conceptual trade-off plot: model storage versus behavior retention, with no unreported results.
Feedback-loop diagram linking model compression to future AI systems.
paper_title: CompressionBench: How can your coding agents compress LLMs?
paper_authors: Xinrui Zhong, Zhifeng Li, Zhiming Wang, Yongqi Liu, Shanglin Yang
